mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the model to have applications with statuses that lack corresponding audit entries. The AuditCompleteness assertion directly checks that every status has exactly one audit entry; without the fact, Alloy will construct a counterexample where an application has a status but no audit entry.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some app: Application | app.status = Approved and no ae: AuditEntry | ae.application = app and ae.new_status = Approved }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows officers to approve applications where they are the applicant. The FR_013 and NoSelfMutation assertions verify that this never happens; without the fact, Alloy will find a counterexample with an officer deciding their own application.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfApprovalViolation { some ae: AuditEntry, app: Application | ae.application = app and ae.actor_role = Officer and ae.new_status = Approved and ae.actor = app.applicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows any officer to patch any application, even if they are not assigned. The FR_012 assertion verifies that status changes only come from the assigned officer; without the fact, Alloy will construct a counterexample with an unassigned officer changing status.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AssignedOfficerViolation { some ae: AuditEntry, app: Application | ae.application = app and ae.actor_role = Officer and ae.new_status = UnderReview and ae.actor != app.assigned_officer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows invalid status transitions such as pending → approved (skipping under_review). The FR_009 assertion verifies that only the documented transitions occur; without the fact, Alloy will find a counterexample with an invalid transition.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InvalidTransitionViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.prev_status = Pending and ae.new_status = Approved }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the permission matrix to be undefined or incorrect. The LeastPrivilege, FR_003, and FR_005 assertions verify the correctness of role-operation permissions; without the fact, Alloy will construct a model where forbidden operations appear to be allowed.

Removing this fact allows applicants to have multiple in-flight applications simultaneously. The FR_008 assertion verifies the one-in-flight constraint; without the fact, Alloy will find a counterexample with duplicate pending/under_review applications for the same applicant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MultipleInFlightViolation { some disj app1, app2: Application, u: User | app1.applicant = u and app2.applicant = u and (app1.status = Pending or app1.status = UnderReview) and (app2.status = Pending or app2.status = UnderReview) }
